title: How fast and how often new .com domains go up for sale
summary: Only 3.5% of brand-new .com domains list for sale in year one, nearly half within 7 days. Data from Afternic, Sedo, and Atom across 2022–2026.
body_markdown:
Most brand-new[.com](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/com) domains are never put up for sale. Out of **25,924,672** brand-new` .com` names registered between November 1, 2024, and October 31, 2025, owners listed **903,544 (3.5%)** as[premium domains for sale](https://instantdomainsearch.com/premium-domains) during their first year (days 0–360), including **768,919 (3%)** with a fixed Buy Now price. The other 96.5% never appeared on a resale marketplace in year one.


When people do buy a` .com` to flip, they list it almost right away. Out of those 903,544 first-year listings, **241,268 (26.7%)** went up for sale on the **same day** the domain first appeared in the` .com` zone file, and **434,110 (48%)** were listed within seven days. By day 30, **550,948 (61%)** were already on the market, for a median wait of **10 days** from registration to listing.


That low, front-loaded resale rate also puts` .com` ’s recent growth in context. In our study on[whether .com is still growing](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/is-com-still-growing) , the` .com` zone hit a record 168.45 million domains in October 2026 as brand-new registrations jumped 24.5% in a year. From November 2025 through September 2026, the share of new` .com` domains listed with a Buy Now price in their first 30 days fell from **1.87%** in 2025 to **1.28%** . We compared 10 years of daily` .com` zone files in Instant History with daily listings from Afternic, Sedo, Atom, GoDaddy, SnapNames, Sav, BrandBucket, Venture, and archived Dan.com records through October 31, 2026, to see how fast new` .com` domains go up for sale, what sellers ask for them, and what share of expired domains end up on the aftermarket.


## How fast do new .com domains go up for sale?


Domain investors connect their registrar accounts to marketplaces or point new names at sales landers during checkout, so listings pile up in the first week. Among the 25,924,672 brand-new` .com` names from our 2025 window, **321,755** were listed for sale by the day after registration (days 0–1), making up **35.6%** of all first-year listings. Daily new listings dropped from 241,268 on day zero to 80,487 on day one, 37,175 on day two, and 23,681 on day three. From there, additions slowed from roughly 2,400 domains a day in month two to about 850 a day across months seven through 12.


Afternic and Sedo handle nearly all early` .com` resale supply. Counting the first marketplace to list each domain, Afternic recorded **494,466 (54.7%)** first-year` .com` listings and Sedo recorded **407,602 (45.1%)** , while curated brand marketplaces such as Atom ( **1,410** ) accounted for the rest. Most sellers posted a set price rather than waiting for bids. Out of the 550,948 domains listed within 30 days, **480,435 (87.2%)** carried a Buy Now price and **70,370 (12.8%)** used Make Offer.

Only **84** of those 550,948 first-month listings (0.015%) were eligible for instant automated delivery. Under ICANN’s[Transfer Policy](https://www.icann.org/resources/pages/transfer-policy-2024-02-21-en) , registrars block new domains from moving to another registrar for 60 days after registration. Afternic’s Fast Transfer network and SedoMLS require that 60-day lock to clear before turning on automated delivery, so any` .com` sold in its first two months must move between accounts at the seller’s current registrar or wait until day 61. Right on **day 60** , new instant-transfer listings jumped from single digits to **451 domains in one day** , reaching **4,059** by day 90 and **27,508** by day 360.


## Owner listings vs. the one-year expiration wave


Tracking those same 2025` .com` names past day 360 shows why raw marketplace totals can mislead you. Between days 355 and 360, about 1,150 domains appeared on a marketplace for the first time each day. On **day 365** , one year after registration, first-time appearances jumped more than 70-fold to **84,455** in a single day, and **84,013 (99.5%)** of them were unpriced Sedo Make Offer pages placed by registrars on newly expired domains.


An even bigger wave arrived five weeks later, when registrar renewal grace periods ended. Across **days 401 through 407** (36 to 42 days after expiration, right before registrars delete unpaid domains), **2,338,547** domains from the 2025 group appeared on Afternic for the first time, peaking at **829,787 on day 404** . Not every late-2025 domain had reached that point by our October 31, 2026 cutoff (all 25.92 million had reached day 365, names registered through September 22 had reached day 404, and names registered through September 6 had reached day 420). Even with those last weeks still unfolding, counting days 361 through 420 makes it look as if **13.6%** of new` .com` domains went up for sale (3.54 million names), when three-quarters of those listings came from expired-domain liquidation. Among earlier brand-new` .com` domains from May 2024 through April 2025 (24.05 million names, all past day 450), post-expiry feeds pushed the raw total on owner marketplaces to **15.2%** by day 420 and **15.6%** by day 450.


While only **3.5%** of brand-new` .com` domains are listed by their owners during year one, **more than half (51.5%)** of the brand-new` .com` names that were gone from the zone by day 450 passed through registrar sales pages or expiry auctions during days 361–450, and **92.2%** appeared on at least one aftermarket or backorder feed. Among the **12,062,230** brand-new` .com` names from May 2024 through April 2025 that were absent from the` .com` zone at day 450, **22.1%** appeared on Afternic or Sedo resale pages during days 361–450 and **40.7%** entered registrar expiry auctions on GoDaddy or SnapNames before deletion (with some listed in both places). Once unsold names entered Verisign’s five-day deletion queue, drop-catching services SnapNames and Sav listed **86.3%** for backorder. Those day-450 zone-absence counts leave out expired names that someone else re-registered before day 450 and include domains taken down early or renewed without nameservers, which make up most of the 7.8% with no year-end expiry listing. Across all **32.54 million**` .com` domains of any age that left the zone for more than 90 days between May 2025 and April 2026, **46.5%** entered registrar expiry sales or auctions and **86.2%** appeared on at least one aftermarket or backorder feed.

Registrar parking pages can also swell unpriced Make Offer counts mid-year without any change in investor demand. Looking only at priced 30-day Buy Now listings filters out that noise. Priced 30-day listings fell from **1.53%** in 2022 to **0.80%** in 2024, rose to **1.87%** in 2025 after GoDaddy merged Dan.com’s inventory into Afternic’s priced feed, and eased to **1.28%** across the 29.03 million brand-new` .com` names registered from November 2025 through September 2026. Total 30-day listings briefly spiked in December 2025 and July 2026 when registrar parking batches added roughly 800,000 unpriced Make Offer pages on ordinary customer domains, including developer test sites, local businesses, and Korean and Chinese IDNs.

## Which new .com names get listed, and at what prices?


Short names and trending keywords draw far more domain flippers than everyday business names. Because every two-, three-, and four-letter` .com` was taken years ago, the 193,333 brand-new` .com` names of five characters or fewer in 2025 were mostly coined five-letter strings. Investors listed **15.7%** of those short names within 30 days ( **20.1%** within 360 days) and **8.7%** of six- and seven-letter names, with high-volume sellers pricing many of them near **$368** . Listing rates dropped to **2.7%** for eight- to 10-letter names (median Buy Now price **$1,890** ), **1.9%** for 11- to 14-letter names (median **$2,000** ), **1.4%** for 15-plus-letter names (median **$2,699** ), **1.2%** for names with numbers, and **0.47%** for hyphenated` .com` domains.


AI buzzwords attracted the heaviest speculation in our archive. During the 2023 chatbot wave, **17.2%** of brand-new` .com` names containing` gpt` went up for sale within 30 days ( **24%** within 360 days) at a **$5,000** median asking price, **10 times** the rate of ordinary` .com` names (1.69%). When startups shifted from chatbots to AI agents in 2025 and 2026, domain flippers followed. In 2025, **22.6%** of brand-new` .com` names containing` agent` ( **28.1%** within 360 days) were listed within 30 days at a **$4,999** median price. From November 2025 through September 2026, **18%** of new` agent`` .com` names went up for sale within 30 days while their median asking price doubled to **$9,995** . Names starting or ending with` ai` had a **7.8%** 30-day listing rate in 2025 and **6.8%** from November 2025 through September 2026 (median **$4,885** ), echoing the shift in[USPTO trademark statistics and AI filing trends](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/are-trademark-filings-growing) .


Everyday app names moved the other way. Brand-new` .com` domains starting with` get` ,` try` ,` use` , or` build` or ending with` app` ,` labs` ,` studio` , or` dev` reached **834,343** registrations in 2025 (counting hyphenated and AI-word combinations, compared with 758,906 unhyphenated non-AI names in our` .com` growth study) and **1,228,656** from November 2025 through September 2026. Only **1.16%** of that 2025 group went up for sale within 30 days ( **2.13%** within 360 days), **lower** than plain non-tech` .com` domains (2.02% in 30 days). Zone files and marketplace feeds cannot tell a live app from an unused domain, so they do not show how many of those names launched websites. They do show that people registering` try` or` labs` domains rarely put them up for resale.


## How many dropped .com domains get picked up and relisted?


Once an expired` .com` finishes deleting and returns to open registration, most names stay unclaimed, while the ones that get picked up feed a disproportionate share of the resale market. Across **13,504,599**` .com` domains confirmed in Verisign’s pending-delete queue between October 1, 2024, and September 30, 2025, **78.8% (10.65 million)** were still unregistered a full year later. Roughly one in five, **21.2% (2,859,104 domains)** , got picked up again within a year, split almost evenly between **10.1% (1.36 million)** caught right at the drop (within 10 days of entering pending delete) and **11.1% (1.50 million)** registered later in the year. Out of all 13.50 million dropped` .com` domains, **4.9% (666,919 domains)** ended up listed for resale by their new owner within that year ( **23.3%** of the names that got picked up, including **31.5%** of immediate drop-catches versus **16%** of later registrations). Checking all 36.72 million` .com` domains that left the zone for at least 35 days over the same period gives nearly the same result, with **22.2%** picked up within a year and **5.2%** ( **23.2%** of pickups) listed for sale.


Domain age shapes both how often a dropped` .com` gets picked up and how long sellers keep it. Among **5.42 million** brand-new` .com` names from May through October 2024 that deleted after just one year, only **7.6% (410,992)** got picked up again within nine months ( **2.6%** at the drop), though **26.7%** of those pickups ( **2%** of first-year drops) still went up for sale. Across all **8,124,140**` .com` domains returning to the zone in 2025 after more than 90 days away, the group covered in our guide on[how to check domain age](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-to-check-domain-age) , **11.09% (901,161 domains)** went up for sale within 360 days ( **7.01%** within 30 days), matching the first-year resale volume of all 25.92 million brand-new` .com` names combined (901,161 vs. 903,544).


To see what happens after the first year ends, we followed **31,654,649**` .com` domains registered between May 1, 2024, and April 30, 2025, out to **450 days** (about 15 months), once first-year expiration, grace, redemption, and deletion windows had closed.

Only **33.5%** of brand-new` .com` domains listed in their first week were still active in the` .com` zone at day 450, meaning **two-thirds (66.5%)** had disappeared from DNS, compared with **50.5%** still active among brand-new names that were never listed. By contrast, **64.3%** of previously owned` .com` domains listed within 30 days (243,187 of 378,333) were still active at day 450, nearly double the rate of brand-new flips. The zone file tracks domains with working nameservers rather than registrar billing records, so a renewed domain without nameservers drops out of the count, a deleted domain someone else registers before day 450 comes back in, and an active domain may have sold to a new owner. Even so, the 31-point gap between brand-new flips (33.5%) and previously owned` .com` names (64.3%) matches the economics in our guide to[buying and selling domain names](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/buying-and-selling-domain-names) , where investors pay more at drop auctions for older names and hold them for years.


## How to find domains for sale or check whether a listing might expire


Because listings are split across Afternic, Sedo, Atom, GoDaddy, and auction houses, checking one registrar misses nearly half of the` .com` names on the market. Search[premium domains for sale](https://instantdomainsearch.com/premium-domains) on Instant Domain Search as you type, or[browse domains for sale by budget, length, and quality score](https://instantdomainsearch.com/premium-domains/search) to compare Buy Now prices, instant-transfer names, auctions, and Make Offer listings in one place. Before making an offer, run a free[domain appraisal](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-appraisal) to compare the asking price against past sales, and check our[top domain sales of 2026](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/top-domain-sales-2026) tracker for verified public deals.


When the` .com` you want has a four-figure price tag on a parked page, check its registration history in the[Domain age checker](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-age-checker) and its expiration date in[domain research](https://instantdomainsearch.com/research) before paying up. If the domain was registered for the first time in the past year with no prior history, two-thirds of similar first-week flips leave the` .com` zone by month 15, and[expired domains](https://instantdomainsearch.com/expired-domains) tracks expiring and newly deleted names if the owner lets it go. For more on weighing older domains against fresh registrations, read our guide to[buying, valuing, and flipping domain names](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/so-you-want-to-buy-domain-names) and our breakdown of[how much a domain name costs](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-much-does-a-domain-name-cost) .


If you would rather launch today for a standard $10–$20 registration fee, check open names instantly on[Instant Domain Search](https://instantdomainsearch.com/) or test ideas in the[domain generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-generator) and[business name generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/business-name-generator) . Developers using Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can connect our free[Domain Search MCP](https://instantdomainsearch.com/mcp) to check` .com` availability, aftermarket prices, and[US trademark search](https://instantdomainsearch.com/trademark-search) records inside chat.


## Frequently asked questions


### What percentage of newly registered .com domains go up for sale?


Out of 25,924,672 brand-new` .com` names that entered Verisign’s daily zone file between November 1, 2024, and October 31, 2025, owners listed 3.5% (903,544 domains) on a resale marketplace such as Afternic, Sedo, or Atom during their first year (days 0–360), including 3% (768,919) with a fixed Buy Now price. Previously owned` .com` domains re-registered after more than 90 days out of DNS went up for sale more than three times as often, at 11.1% within 360 days.


### How fast can you list and sell a newly registered domain?


You can list a new` .com` for sale on day zero, and 26.7% of all first-year` .com` resale listings go live on the same day the domain enters the zone file (48% within seven days). Under ICANN’s Transfer Policy, however, registrars lock new domains from moving to another registrar for 60 days. Until day 60, a domain cannot use automated instant-transfer networks, so an early buyer must take delivery in an account at the seller’s current registrar or wait for the 60-day lock to end.


### What percentage of expired .com domains end up on the aftermarket?


Among the 12,062,230 brand-new` .com` names from May 2024 through April 2025 that were absent from the` .com` zone at day 450, 51.5% (6.21 million) entered registrar sales pages or expiry auctions during days 361–450 (22.1% on Afternic or Sedo and 40.7% in GoDaddy or SnapNames registrar auctions), and 86.3% (10.41 million) appeared on SnapNames or Sav pending-delete backorder lists, for 92.2% across all feeds combined. Across all 32.54 million` .com` domains of any age that left the zone for more than 90 days between May 2025 and April 2026, 46.5% entered registrar expiry sales or auctions and 86.2% hit at least one aftermarket or backorder feed.


### What percentage of dropped .com domains get picked up again and listed for sale?


Across 13,504,599` .com` domains confirmed in pending delete between October 2024 and September 2025, 21.2% (2.86 million) were registered again within one year (10.1% caught right at the drop and 11.1% registered later in the year), while 78.8% stayed unregistered. Nearly a quarter of the names that got picked up (23.3%, or 4.9% of all dropped` .com` domains) were listed for resale by their new owner within that year, led by 31.5% among domains caught right at the drop.


### Do domain flippers keep unsold .com domains after year one?


Much less often on brand-new registrations than on older drops. Among brand-new` .com` domains registered between May 2024 and April 2025 and listed for sale in their first week, only 33.5% were still active in the` .com` zone 450 days later (66.5% had left DNS), compared with 64.3% among previously owned` .com` domains listed within 30 days. Zone files measure active nameservers rather than billing renewals, so renewed domains without nameservers drop out while deleted names someone else registers before day 450 reappear.

Instant History pairs daily changes in Verisign’s` .com` zone file with daily marketplace feeds. To separate owner resale listings from expiration auctions, first-year counts track new listings across Afternic, Sedo, Atom, Dan.com, BrandBucket, Venture, and Epik (excluding expired-domain auction feeds) across days` 0–360` after a domain first enters the` .com` zone, and leave out names that still carried an old marketplace listing from a prior owner on registration day (80,695 names in 2025). GoDaddy folded Dan.com’s unpriced feed into Afternic in late 2024, and our BrandBucket, Venture, and Sav feeds paused in September 2026, while Afternic, Sedo, Atom, GoDaddy, and SnapNames ran daily through October 31, 2026. Price medians use each domain’s first non-zero US dollar Buy Now price below the $200 million placeholder cap.
